title: Choose shrten’s visual world
question: Which product world should carry the homepage shortening workflow?

options.label: The Routing Proof
options.lineage: letterpress job tickets and print-shop routing slips
options.thesis: Every short link becomes a compact routing proof: destination, controls, and issued code on one working sheet.
options.viewport: A full-width working sheet leads from the long destination through optional routing controls to an issued short code, with the live form as the page’s main piece of typography.
options.risk: The tactile language could feel nostalgic if status, focus, and validation are not kept exact.

raised.raise: A fixed status line gives every validation and result state an unmistakable place.
The selected route receives absolute contrast while supporting information recedes.
Every optional control is named literally and earns its position.
Advanced configuration unfolds as a deliberate second depth, not a hidden afterthought.

options.label: Dispatch Label
options.lineage: courier airway bills and destination labels
options.thesis: A long destination is packed, routed, and issued as a compact address label ready to travel.
options.viewport: The destination field spans the page like a shipping address, while the generated short URL lands in a detachable result strip with one clear copy action.
options.risk: The metaphor is immediately legible but can drift toward ordinary logistics software.

options.label: Midnight Transit
options.lineage: metropolitan rail maps and enamel station signage
options.thesis: The long URL and short URL are two stations on one route, with protection and geo rules as controlled branches.
options.viewport: A disciplined route diagram crosses the working form, brightening from destination station to short-link station when the result arrives.
options.case: It holds product clarity through routing and state, but identifies more with travel than everyday link work.
options.risk: The route metaphor may overstate a simple one-step action if the diagram becomes ornamental.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: Shortening becomes a direct service page: key a destination, set a few route flags, receive an address.
options.viewport: A strict 40-column service screen gives the input, advanced flags, and result separate numbered bands with zero decorative ambiguity.
options.case: It holds scanability and memorable state language, but its retro broadcast culture is less universal than the routing proof.
options.risk: Without ruthless grid discipline it becomes retro novelty instead of a dependable tool.

options.label: Data Field
options.thesis: The URL is compressed as a visible field of bars and indexed data.
options.viewport: A dense monochrome field isolates the active destination and its generated code.
options.case: It loses both audience identification and immediate form clarity for a general-purpose tool.
options.kept: Absolute contrast and a single unambiguous active route.
options.risk: The effect can overwhelm basic input and accessibility needs.

options.label: Certified Noise
options.thesis: Every generated link is stamped, registered, and certified through dense information marks.
options.viewport: A giant destination command cuts through tightly registered controls and result codes.
options.case: It identifies with a narrow design culture and reduces clarity when the core action must stay calm.
options.kept: The courage to use density as structure rather than filling the page with empty space.
options.risk: Information noise conflicts with the trust and ease expected from a utility.

options.label: Industrial Labels
options.thesis: Literal labels and safety marks turn each option into an unmistakable routing instruction.
options.viewport: The form stacks as labeled stockroom zones with one orange action tag.
options.case: It loses product identification because apparel and stockroom cues do not belong to link management.
options.kept: Literal naming and decisive enabled, disabled, and active states.
options.risk: The quotation and hazard grammar can feel mannered in repeated controls.

options.label: Controlled Descent
options.thesis: The simple link stays at the surface while advanced controls descend by deliberate depth.
options.viewport: A vertical depth scale moves from destination to protection and routing controls.
options.case: It supports progressive disclosure but loses both audience identification and the horizontal send-and-receive logic of links.
options.kept: Advanced options become a clearly signposted second depth with an easy return to the core action.
options.risk: Atmosphere could make a fast utility feel slower than it is.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A centered SaaS utility hero and conventional form card, executed with excellent spacing and polish.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar headline, centered URL field, compact feature reassurance, and result card.
canonCard.risk: Immediately understandable but intentionally difficult to distinguish from other URL shorteners.
